english: to be lucky / to get lucky (colloquial)
situation_en: Something went well by pure luck — you caught the delayed train, found the last free table, passed by one point.

example_sentences.de: Da hast du echt Schwein gehabt — der Zug hatte zum Glück Verspätung!
example_sentences.en: You really got lucky there — luckily the train was delayed!

example_sentences.de: Wir haben Schwein gehabt: Das waren die letzten zwei Tickets.
example_sentences.en: We got lucky: those were the last two tickets.

notes: Almost always in the Perfekt: Schwein gehabt! The pig is a German good-luck symbol (das Glücksschwein) — marzipan pigs are given as New Year presents.
related: Glück haben (neutral register), das Glücksschwein, Pech haben (opposite: to be unlucky)

situation_en: Someone is unsure what to do and you offer your opinion on what they should do.

example_sentences.de: Meine Oma gibt mir immer gute Ratschläge.
example_sentences.en: My grandma always gives me good advice.

example_sentences.de: Er gibt gern Ratschläge, ohne gefragt zu werden.
example_sentences.en: He likes giving advice without being asked.

notes: Fixed verb: geben (not machen!). Singular: einen Ratschlag / einen Rat geben. Ask for advice: jemanden um Rat fragen.
related: der Ratschlag (noun), um Rat fragen, der Tipp

english: please stay objective / stick to the facts
situation_en: A discussion is getting emotional or personal and you want to bring it back to the facts.

example_sentences.de: Die Diskussion wurde laut. „Bitte sachlich bleiben!“, sagte die Moderatorin.
example_sentences.en: The discussion got loud. "Please stay objective!", said the moderator.

example_sentences.de: Bleiben wir sachlich: Was sind die Fakten?
example_sentences.en: Let's stick to the facts: what are the facts?

notes: sachlich comes from die Sache (the matter). Core vocabulary for meetings, debates and online discussions. Opposite: persönlich/emotional werden.
related: sachlich (objective), die Sachlichkeit, zur Sache kommen (to get to the point)

english: anyway / be that as it may
situation_en: You want to close a topic, move on, or signal that the details don't matter right now.

example_sentences.de: Wie auch immer — wir müssen jetzt eine Entscheidung treffen.
example_sentences.en: Anyway — we have to make a decision now.

example_sentences.de: Wie auch immer, das Ergebnis bleibt gleich.
example_sentences.en: Be that as it may, the result stays the same.

notes: Discourse marker to change or close a topic — makes conversation flow naturally. Family: was auch immer (whatever), wo auch immer (wherever), wie dem auch sei (formal).
related: jedenfalls (in any case), egal (doesn't matter), wie dem auch sei

situation_en: You and someone else just made an arrangement or deal and you seal it.

example_sentences.de: „Ich koche, du spülst?“ — „Abgemacht!“
example_sentences.en: "I cook, you do the dishes?" — "Deal!"

example_sentences.de: Also morgen um zehn? Abgemacht!
example_sentences.en: So tomorrow at ten? Settled!

notes: Partizip II of abmachen (to arrange/agree on — see Verbs). Used alone as a one-word answer to seal an agreement, like shaking hands verbally.

situation_en: Someone proposes something and you formally give your OK — or you ask someone for theirs.

example_sentences.de: Bist du mit dem Plan einverstanden?
example_sentences.en: Do you agree with the plan?

example_sentences.de: „Treffen wir uns um acht?“ — „Einverstanden.“
example_sentences.en: "Shall we meet at eight?" — "Agreed."

notes: Pattern: einverstanden sein mit + Dativ. As a standalone answer it is slightly more formal than Abgemacht. Noun: das Einverständnis (consent).

english: as much / as little / as often as possible
situation_en: You want to express 'to the maximum degree that is possible' without the long so-…-wie-möglich construction.

example_sentences.de: Trink möglichst viel Wasser — das ist gesund.
example_sentences.en: Drink as much water as possible — it's healthy.

example_sentences.de: Ich versuche, möglichst oft zu Fuß zu gehen.
example_sentences.en: I try to walk as often as possible.

notes: möglichst + adjective/adverb compresses 'so X wie möglich': möglichst schnell = so schnell wie möglich. Extremely common in instructions and advice.
related: so … wie möglich, möglich (possible), die Möglichkeit

english: to get confused / to get mixed up
situation_en: Too many names, numbers or similar words — and your head loses track.

example_sentences.de: Bei den vielen Namen komme ich durcheinander.
example_sentences.en: With all these names I get confused.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin mit den Terminen völlig durcheinander gekommen.
example_sentences.en: I got the appointments completely mixed up.

notes: durcheinander = mixed up, in disarray. Related: das Durcheinander (chaos/mess), etwas durcheinanderbringen (to mix things up). Perfekt with sein: Ich bin durcheinander gekommen.
related: das Durcheinander, durcheinanderbringen, verwechseln (to confuse two things)

english: I feel like … / I'm in the mood for …
situation_en: Saying what you feel like doing or having right now.

example_sentences.de: Heute ist mir nach Pizza.
example_sentences.en: I feel like pizza today.

example_sentences.de: Mir ist heute nicht nach Feiern.
example_sentences.en: I'm not in the mood for partying today.

notes: mir (Dativ) + ist + nach + Dativ. Same meaning: Ich habe Lust auf … (+ Akk).

situation_en: Asking for someone's opinion about something.

example_sentences.de: Was hältst du von der Idee?
example_sentences.en: What do you think of the idea?

example_sentences.de: Was hältst du davon, ins Kino zu gehen?
example_sentences.en: What do you think about going to the cinema?

notes: halten von + Dativ = to have an opinion of. Answers: Ich halte viel/nichts davon.

situation_en: Saying what you are busy doing right now.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin gerade dabei zu kochen.
example_sentences.en: I'm in the middle of cooking.

example_sentences.de: Wir sind gerade dabei, die Wohnung zu putzen.
example_sentences.en: We're in the middle of cleaning the flat.

notes: dabei sein + zu-Infinitiv. German has no -ing form; this (or just 'gerade' + verb) expresses it.

situation_en: Something brings back a memory.

example_sentences.de: Das erinnert mich an meinen Urlaub.
example_sentences.en: That reminds me of my holiday.

example_sentences.de: Dieses Lied erinnert mich an dich.
example_sentences.en: This song reminds me of you.

notes: jemanden an + Akkusativ erinnern. Reflexive: sich an etwas erinnern = to remember.

situation_en: Reacting with enthusiasm to good news.

example_sentences.de: Du hast den Job bekommen? Klasse!
example_sentences.en: You got the job? Great!

example_sentences.de: Das war ein klasse Abend!
example_sentences.en: That was a great evening!

notes: Colloquial praise. As an adjective it never takes endings: ein klasse Abend. B1/B2 alternative: ausgezeichnet.

situation_en: Saying that one thing grows as another grows.

example_sentences.de: Je mehr ich übe, desto besser spreche ich Deutsch.
example_sentences.en: The more I practise, the better I speak German.

example_sentences.de: Je älter er wird, desto ruhiger wird er.
example_sentences.en: The older he gets, the calmer he becomes.

notes: je + comparative … verb at the END; desto + comparative + verb SECOND. umso can replace desto.

situation_en: Including two things equally.

example_sentences.de: Ich spreche sowohl Deutsch als auch Englisch.
example_sentences.en: I speak both German and English.

example_sentences.de: Sowohl die Kinder als auch die Eltern waren begeistert.
example_sentences.en: Both the children and the parents were thrilled.

notes: Links two equal parts. Also possible: sowohl … wie auch.

situation_en: Only one of two options is possible.

example_sentences.de: Du kannst entweder Tee oder Kaffee haben.
example_sentences.en: You can have either tea or coffee.

example_sentences.de: Entweder kommst du mit, oder du bleibst zu Hause.
example_sentences.en: Either you come along or you stay at home.

notes: Only one of the two. Entweder at the start: the verb follows directly (Entweder kommst du …).

situation_en: Excluding both of two things.

example_sentences.de: Er hat weder Zeit noch Geld.
example_sentences.en: He has neither time nor money.

example_sentences.de: Ich trinke weder Kaffee noch Tee.
example_sentences.en: I drink neither coffee nor tea.

notes: Already negative — no nicht or kein needed.

situation_en: Adding a second, stronger point.

example_sentences.de: Sie ist nicht nur klug, sondern auch freundlich.
example_sentences.en: She is not only clever but also friendly.

example_sentences.de: Er spricht nicht nur Deutsch, sondern auch Japanisch.
example_sentences.en: He speaks not only German but also Japanese.

notes: Stresses the second part. Comma before sondern.

situation_en: Conceding a point, then contrasting it.

example_sentences.de: Das Auto ist zwar teuer, aber sehr gut.
example_sentences.en: The car is expensive, admittedly, but very good.

example_sentences.de: Ich habe zwar wenig Zeit, aber ich helfe dir.
example_sentences.en: I don't have much time, it's true, but I'll help you.

notes: Concede, then contrast. doch or jedoch can replace aber.

english: on the one hand … on the other hand
literal: on one side … on the other side
situation_en: Weighing two sides of a decision.

example_sentences.de: Einerseits möchte ich reisen, andererseits muss ich sparen.
example_sentences.en: On the one hand I want to travel, on the other hand I have to save.

example_sentences.de: Einerseits ist die Stadt laut, andererseits ist sie spannend.
example_sentences.en: On the one hand the city is noisy, on the other hand it's exciting.

notes: Both words take position 1, so the verb follows directly. The single words are also in the Adverbs module.
